changes.after: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, had to enter passenger service by its 8 December 2026 longstop date; contractor LINXS now says service could begin on 6 January 2027, with "no assurances" it will not slip again.
changes.before: The 2.25-mile LAX people mover, 99% complete but years late, must enter passenger service by its project longstop date of 8 December 2026 or its developer LINXS risks a technical default on $1.2 billion of bonds.

changes.after:
• In a 16 September disclosure filing, LINXS said it will need time beyond the 8 December completion deadline; if all goes well the train could be running by 6 January 2027, though "there can be no assurances" the date will not slip further
  • Before opening, the train must pass 30 consecutive days of testing, an independent review and an assessment by Los Angeles World Airports, and a utility agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power must be completed
  • Recent testing was paused twice to fix track components that "accommodate movement resulting from temperature changes, seismic activity and normal structural behavior"
  • Bondholders agreed to push the lender longstop date on the SkyLink bonds back to December, lining it up with the construction longstop and averting a technical default that would have been triggered in October
  • Fitch's Seth Lehman said the best case is a 30-day commissioning test starting by the end of September, a utility agreement and public service beginning by December 8, "but it's very tight"; a delay beyond December would need LAWA's consent
  • The project is more than 99% complete, and a dispute over the interconnection agreement with the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, which LAX has not signed, remains; the developer has money for debt service only into early to mid-2027
  • The California Municipal Finance Authority issued $1.2 billion of bonds for LINXS in 2018; Fitch cut them to BB in July 2026 after LINXS sued the city on July 9
  • Construction was first due in March 2023; systems demonstration testing began on April 21, 2026, and the project longstop date is December 8, 2026
  • An August 2026 report had the $3.34 billion system targeting passenger service in October 2026

Notable features

  • A 2.25-mile driverless train with six stations linking the terminals, the LAX/Metro Transit Center and the Rental Car Center

• The pin's forecast comes from Peter Zeihan's video "The 2nd Holodomor: A Pending Genocide" (Zeihan on Geopolitics, 24 January 2023), which argues that Russia was gearing up for a second Holodomor by deliberately destroying Ukraine's agricultural production
  • Russia let the Black Sea Grain Initiative lapse on 17 July 2023; by then the deal had moved nearly 33 million tonnes of grain and other food from Ukrainian ports to more than 40 countries, 57% of grain exports going to developing countries, with Egypt fifth by number of shipments in 2022; UN Secretary-General Guterres said the deals had helped cut food prices by over 23 per cent since March 2022 and that the decision "will strike a blow to people in need everywhere"
  • Russia then struck grain storage and loading facilities in Ukraine's Black Sea and Danube ports and warned that ships entering Ukrainian waters could be treated as legitimate targets; a 23 August 2023 drone attack on Izmail destroyed 13,000 tons of grain bound for Egypt and Romania, and Egypt's President el-Sisi joined other African leaders at the July 2023 Russia-Africa Summit in urging Putin to renew the deal
  • The Black Sea did not become a no-go zone: Ukraine opened its own corridor, the container ship Joseph Schulte left Odesa through it on 16 August 2023, and by 31 December 2023 Ukraine had moved 13 million tons by sea on 430 vessels
  • Egypt's annual urban inflation reached a record 38% in September 2023, driven by vegetable prices (up 19.2% on the month after one of the hottest summers on record) and a currency that had lost more than half its value since March 2022, while bread and cereal prices fell 1.3% from August

• The Francis Scott Key Bridge (I-695, Baltimore) opened 23 March 1977; a steel continuous truss 8,636 ft long with a 1,200 ft main span
  • On 26 March 2024 the container ship MV Dali lost power and struck a support pier, collapsing the main spans; six maintenance workers died and two were rescued, and a mayday call let police halt traffic
  • Replacement plans: in May 2024 officials projected $1.7-1.9 billion and completion in fall 2028; Kiewit was named progressive design-builder in August 2024 with opening "expected in Fall 2028"
  • The 2028 target has since been superseded: on 17 November 2025 the Maryland Transportation Authority raised the estimate to $4.3-5.2 billion with an anticipated open-to-traffic date in late 2030, citing much higher material costs, a larger pier protection system and a main span lengthened to 1,665 ft
  • On 28 April 2026 MDTA dropped Kiewit from Phase 2 construction because its proposal far exceeded the state's independent cost estimates; by August 2026 the state planned to award the main overwater contract in June 2027 and still had "a goal of the end of 2030", now asking for completion "as near to December 31, 2030 as practicable" rather than the 2024 requirement of "no later than October 15, 2028"
  • Funding includes a $350 million Chubb insurance payout, a $101.98 million DOJ settlement with the Dali's owner and manager, and a 100 percent federal Emergency Relief share set by law in December 2024

  • The first phase, lasting until 2030, was to cost SAR 1.2 trillion (about US$320 billion) per the crown prince in 2022

• Samsung Thailand's newsroom roadmap sets 28 September 2026 as the start of the One UI 9 rollout for the Galaxy S25 series and the Galaxy Z Fold7 and Z Flip7
  • The Galaxy S25 line covered includes the S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 Edge and S25 FE
  • This follows the stable One UI 9 debut in South Korea on 16 September 2026 with the Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra, after the software first shipped on the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Fold8 and Flip8 and out of the box on the Galaxy S26 FE

  • Sammy Fans reported on 22 September 2026 that the Thai page later dropped a fixed date altogether in favour of "Within September", which the site framed as a change to the announcement timing rather than a confirmed delay of the update itself

  • Now Brief gains Generative and Editable Cards so users can build their own daily-summary cards across health, weather and video
  • Now Nudge surfaces context-aware suggestions in the flow of use, such as pulling up reservation details or saving a shared location from a conversation, working with Samsung Messages, Google Messages and Google Chat
  • Creative Studio suggests image-generation prompts tied to upcoming events such as a friend's birthday
  • Interpreter adds a Thread View for reviewing earlier exchanges, with faster Conversation Mode translation and quicker playback on compatible Galaxy Buds
  • Document Scan handles curved book pages and folded corners with less manual correction, adds large-screen-optimised views and an improved Finger Eraser; Voice Recorder structures summaries with headings and tables
  • Security and privacy additions: a Security Brief inside Now Brief flagging malware, unknown-source apps and unnecessary permissions; on-device AI Privacy Alerts; and Scam Detection expanding to Japan, Canada and India
  • Privacy Alerts support spans the Galaxy S26/S25/S24/S23 families (including FE models), Z Fold8 Ultra/Fold8/Flip8 down to Fold5/Flip5, and Tab S11, S10 and S9 tablets
  • Warranty and Care moves device support into Settings, covering warranty checks across linked devices, self-diagnostics, repair estimates and Samsung Care+ management or service booking, with availability varying by region

• Amazon says it now has enough satellites in orbit to begin “initial service” of its Leo internet-from-space network later in 2026, though it has not launched the service for consumers and government customers yet
  • The milestone came with a United Launch Alliance Atlas V launch of 29 satellites at about 12:30 a.m. ET on Thursday 2 July 2026
  • The two reports of that launch give different constellation totals: CNBC says it brought Amazon to “more than 390 satellites”, while Light Reading says Amazon Leo announced it had deployed 396
  • Chris Weber, the executive leading Leo's consumer, enterprise and government businesses, said the constellation is “enough to support continuous service across initial latitudes” and that “we've completed enough launches for initial service this yr, and future missions just add coverage and capacity”, with “lots of work ahead - including raising all these new satellites to their assigned altitude”
  • The timing has slipped: Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter targeted commercial availability in “mid-2026”, a target he repeated in May, and Amazon now says only “later this year”; Light Reading calls the exact timing “somewhat squishy”. Amazon's own FAQ says only that it will “roll out Amazon Leo service more widely in 2026”
  • Initial commercial service will likely be limited to users in certain geographies, and Amazon has announced neither pricing plans nor where the service will first be available
  • The links date the enterprise phase differently: CNBC and Amazon's FAQ say an enterprise preview for select businesses began in November (2025), while TNW says the service “entered enterprise beta on April 8, 2026” and separately that a business preview opened to select enterprise partners shortly after the November 2025 rebrand
  • The service was rebranded from Project Kuiper, announced in 2019, to Amazon Leo in November 2025; Amazon says the Kuiper name was retired on 13 November 2025, and that Leo is an Amazon business in its Devices and Services division, not part of Blue Origin
  • Amazon aims at a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites — the FCC approved its Generation 2 constellation in February 2026, clearing a potential 7,727-satellite network on top of the 3,236-satellite Generation 1 licence
  • Deployment has run far behind the licence: Generation 1 required 1,618 satellites in orbit and operational by 30 July 2026, and Amazon had roughly 210 to 241 in orbit in early April 2026, having told the FCC it expected about 700 by that July
  • Amazon filed for an extension in January 2026 citing a “shortage in the near-term availability” of rockets, and the FCC granted a 24-month extension on the first half of the constellation while retaining the 100% deployment milestone of 30 July 2029
  • A further setback came in May, when a Blue Origin New Glenn exploded on the launchpad during a hot-fire test days before it was to carry a batch of Amazon satellites
  • The next Leo mission moves to ULA's Vulcan heavy-lift rocket, “which will carry even larger Leo payloads and help increase our deployment rate” — 40-plus satellites per launch — after Atlas V closed its Leo campaign having launched 224 satellites across eight missions with a 100% success rate

  • The satellites are connected by high-speed optical links and relay traffic to a ground network of gateway antennas, fibre and internet connection points; Amazon says flying closer to Earth gives lower latency than traditional satellite internet, suiting video calls, gaming and high-definition streaming
  • Amazon's Kirkland, Washington factory can build up to five satellites per day, and satellites are integrated with rockets at its Kennedy Space Center processing facility
  • Three terminals are planned: Leo Nano at seven inches square and 2.2 pounds rated to 100 Mbps, Leo Pro at eleven inches square and 5.3 pounds priced under $400 and rated to 400 Mbps, and Leo Ultra, a 43-pound enterprise unit rated at 1 Gbps down and 400 Mbps up
